topIssues.title: [L2CM Upgrades] Implement Bundle Canoniclization process
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
I’m proposing a solution between A and B. We want to have a manual trigger to update the bundled NUT per hardfork, but also want enough automation and CI checks to avoid human error. My proposed workflow:

- Command `just update-nuts <fork>` ensures the latest nuts are built, then copies the `nuts-current.json`  to a predetermined location, e.g. `op-core/nuts/nuts-<fork>.json`
    - This may update the NUTs for fork `<fork>`, overwriting the old one. This will clearly be visible in the PR diff.
    - This script invocation can also do other sanity checks, e.g. that the `<fork>`  is a valid one defined in `op-core/forks`.
    - We may also add to this script, and CI checks below, a way to freeze NUTs updates in some way, so nobody ever accidentally updates an old NUTs bundle. Could be something as simple as a `var FrozenFork` in the `forks` package, or a string in a file `frozen_fork.txt` in `op-core/nuts` that can be reused by the Rust stack as well.
    - Even better, add a proper fork lock file `op-core/nuts/fock_lock.toml` with content like
        
        ```toml
        jovian = 1ab2c3...
        karst = 4d5e6f...
        ...
        ```
        
        - where every line commits to the bundle hash (tbd what that exactly is, maybe just file sha256)
        - If a fork is not locked here yet, it’s allowed to be updated. once it’s locked, CI checks that it cannot be updated. Would require manual edits to the lock to update again.
        - We’d set the lock once we write the gov post.
- Implementation detail, but to sketch what’s happening with this file: it’s embedded into the Go build using `//go:embed` and the developers for `<fork>` have to call a `func generateNUTs(fork forks.Name) ([]hexutil.Bytes, error)` inside `~~FetchingAttributesBuilder~~.PreparePayloadAttributes` (where also the upgrade txs are currently built). We could in the future automate this further by iterating over all forks with `forks.From(<first-fork-with-NUTs>)`, but this is getting too detailed…
- Note: has nothing to do with op-node release tags. An update is clearly visible in the PR and via git history. We can also add a code ownership rule that any changes to `op-core/nuts/` require EVM team & Consensus team approval.
- CI actually checks the validity of this copied NUT:
    - if the current PR *changes* any file in `op-core/nuts/nuts-<fork>.json`, this changed file has to be equal to the `nuts-current.json` that is built from the current commit.
    - if the current PR doesn’t change anything in `op-core/nuts/`, it is guaranteed that a previous CI run has validated it, so nothing to check.
- We can an option to use the latest, but we need a way to ensure we don’t actually ship a hard fork that’s still using current-nuts.json. Maybe just require a CLI flag is set in order to activate a hard fork that uses current-nuts.

([Source](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/P-PS-How-to-Bundle-L2-Contracts-into-the-client-with-L2CM-2fcf153ee162807c9a65caf67ca7fdc9?source=copy_link))

topIssues.title: bug(kona): kona-host-client-offline-cannon test crashes due to wrong target spec in cannon-builder:v1.0.0
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed on behalf of @ajsutton.

## Description

The `kona-host-client-offline-cannon` CI job uses `just build-cannon-client` which runs `docker run cannon-builder:v1.0.0 cargo build ...` to cross-compile `kona-client` for MIPS64. The `cannon-builder:v1.0.0` Docker image has a baked-in `mips64-unknown-none.json` target spec with `target-c-int-width: 64` (incorrect — should be `32`).

This causes the kona-client binary to crash immediately when run on cannon:

```
Panic: panicked at kona/crates/protocol/registry/src/superchain.rs:26:42:
Failed to read chain list: Error("missing field `name`", line: 23, column: 3)
```

The test currently **passes** on `develop` because it only checks that cannon VM execution completes (`exited=true`), not that the exit code is successful. The client panics with exit code 2, which counts as "exited".

## Evidence

From the latest successful `kona-host-client-offline-cannon` run on `develop` (CircleCI job #4729278):

```
t=2026-04-02T04:54:03+0000 lvl=info msg="" module=guest stream=stderr text="Panic: panicked at kona/crates/protocol/registry/src/superchain.rs:26:42:\nFailed to read chain list: Error(\"missing field `name`\", line: 23, column: 3)"
t=2026-04-02T04:54:03+0000 lvl=info msg="Execution stopped" module=vm exited=true code=2
```

## Root Cause

The `cannon-builder:v1.0.0` image at `us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/cannon-builder:v1.0.0` has `target-c-int-width: 64` in its baked-in `/mips64-unknown-none.json`. The corrected value (`32`) exists in the source tree at `rust/kona/docker/cannon/mips64-unknown-none.json`. The reproducible prestate Dockerfile (`cannon-repro.dockerfile`) already overrides the baked-in spec, but `build-cannon-client` in `rust/kona/justfile` uses `cannon-builder:v1.0.0` directly without the override.

## Fix

The `build-cannon-client` target should use the corrected target spec from the source tree. This is being addressed as part of ethereum-optimism/optimism#19889 which refactors the kona prestate build to use a single definition. With that change, `build-cannon-client` calls `just build-kona-client-elf` which sets `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` to the corrected spec.

The offline test's witness data and assertions should also be updated to expect a successful block validation (exit code 0) rather than a crash (exit code 2).

topIssues.title: Add L2CM support for op-chain-ops
topIssues.author: 0xniha
topIssues.body:
**Description:**
`interopgen` currently hardcodes `UseL2CM: false` when building L2 genesis (`op-chain-ops/interopgen/deploy.go`, in `GenesisL2`).

This prevents interop/test deployments from enabling the L2 Contract Messenger (L2CM) feature, which gates inclusion of the **ConditionalDeployer** predeploy in L2 genesis.

**Implementation notes**
1. **Config**: Add a way to turn on L2CM for L2 genesis. Options:
   - Add a field to `L2Config` (e.g. `UseL2CM bool`) or
   - Add a world-level or superchain-level flag.
2. **Wire-through**: In `GenesisL2`, pass the configured value into `opcm.L2GenesisInput.UseL2CM` instead of `false`.

topPRs.title: fix(op-reth): detect reth storage layout in InitializationJob
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Running op-reth proofs init on a production OP Mainnet node (synced before reth introduced v2 packed storage) panics with:


index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 32
The panic is in PackedStoredNibbles::from_compact, which always reads buf[32] as the nibble count. On v1-storage nodes, AccountsTrie keys are variable-length (1 nibble per byte, 1–64 bytes). A 1-nibble path is 1 byte — indexing buf[32] panics.

**Tests**

Tested v1 in op mainnet
v2 is being tested in e2e

**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

- Fixes #20394 
- Build on top of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19928

topPRs.title: fix(kona): load DependencySet from embedded registry, oracle as fallback
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`BootInfo::load` (kona-proof-interop) loaded the dependency set only from the preimage oracle, which the real on-chain `PreimageOracle` cannot supply (`local(8)`), so a fault-proof program couldn't complete once interop is active. This adds the embedded-first / oracle-fallback pattern already used for `rollup_configs` and `l1_config`: `kona_registry::DEPENDENCY_SETS` is now a `HashMap<u64, DependencySet>` keyed by L2 chain id and populated at compile time from `etc/depsets.json`. The build script aggregates one `DependencySet` per cluster from the superchain-registry's `[interop.dependencies]` blocks (validating cluster consistency and rejecting dangling members) and merges any custom depsets from `KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS_DIR/depsets.json` with cross-cluster collision detection. `BootInfo::load` does a single embedded lookup against the proof's first chain id and falls back to the oracle when the binary has no embedded depset for that chain. Cross-cluster and partial-coverage proofs aren't checked at boot — they fail downstream when interop message validation rejects messages whose source chain isn't in the chosen depset's `dependencies` map.

To break the `kona-interop ↔ kona-registry` dependency cycle, `DependencySet`/`ChainDependency`/`MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` move to `kona-genesis` (re-exported by `kona-interop` for API compatibility). `ChainConfig` gains an optional `[interop]` field with `serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")` so existing JSON round-trips are unchanged. Wire compatibility with op-supervisor's `StaticConfigDependencySet` is locked in by a fixture round-trip test.

topPRs.title: feat: zk go deployer
topPRs.author: ashitakah
topPRs.body:
## Changed

- **upgrade.go**  
  Added support for `GameTypeZKDisputeGame` (type 10), including the `ZKDisputeGameConfig` struct and ABI encoding required for the OPCM V2 upgrade flow.

- **add_game_type.go**  
  Hooked `ZKDisputeGameType` into the game type registry for devstack environments.

- **chain_intent.go**  
  Introduced `ZKDisputeGameParams` and an optional `ZKDisputeGame` field on `AdditionalDisputeGame`.  
  Added validation in `Check()` to reject any ZK game entry with:
  - zero `Verifier` address  
  - zero `AbsolutePrestate`  
  This prevents silently broken game deployments.

- **devfeatures.go**  
  Added `ZKDisputeGameDevFlag`.  
  The flag is automatically OR-ed into the `DevFeatureBitmap` in `pipeline/implementations.go` whenever any chain intent includes an `AdditionalDisputeGame` with `VMType == VMTypeZK`.  
  This ensures `ZkDisputeGameImpl` is deployed without manual bitmap configuration.

- **pipeline/implementations.go**  
  Auto-enables `ZKDisputeGameDevFlag` when a ZK game is present in any chain’s `AdditionalDisputeGames`, then forwards it to `DeployImplementations`.

- **DeployImplementations.s.sol / VerifyOPCM.s.sol**  
  - Plumbed `zkDisputeGameImpl` through the deploy script `Implementations` struct.  
  - Added it to `validatorGetterChecks` to ensure it is verified against the container during deployment.

- **Remaining files**  
  Added plumbing to read and persist `zkDisputeGameImpl` from `ReadImplementationAddresses` into state.

---

## Why the initial deployment files weren't touched

- `DeployOPChain.s.sol` intentionally registers the ZK game slot with `enabled: false`.  
- ZK is not intended to be activated for new chains at deployment time.  
- Instead, it is enabled on existing chains through the OPCM V2 upgrade path.

topPRs.title: feat(kona): execute NUT bundles at Karst fork activation
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Wires Karst NUT bundle execution into kona-node's payload derivation, matching op-node's behavior.

- `kona-hardforks` gets a `build.rs` that reads `op-core/nuts/bundles/karst_nut_bundle.json` at compile time and emits Rust code constructing the `NutBundle` — keeps the crate `no_std` and serde-free at runtime.
- The `Hardfork` trait grows `upgrade_gas()`; the stateful attributes builder adds that gas to the block gas limit when Karst activates, so upgrade transactions have headroom.
- Test in `forks.rs` updated from `len() == 0` to `len() == 32` to reflect the populated bundle.

## Stacking

Stacked on top of #20062 (PR 1 — NUT bundle types in `op-alloy-consensus`). The first two commits belong to that PR and will drop out on rebase once #20062 merges. Review only `c38d4300d8`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run` in `rust/kona` — 119 passed
- [x] `test_karst_upgrade_txs` asserts 32 transactions
- [x] `test_karst_upgrade_gas` asserts 51_600_000 gas
- [ ] Waiting on #20062 to merge, then rebase onto develop

topPRs.title: feat: migrate Interop activation to L2CM NUT bundle
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrates Interop hardfork activation toward the L2CM NUT bundle path. The branch currently includes:

- Interop NUT bundle generation and committed `op-core/nuts/bundles/interop_nut_bundle.json`
- op-core bundle embedding and fork lock entry
- op-node activation wrappers for `setFeature(INTEROP)` and ETHLiquidity funding
- kona Interop hardfork wrapper implementation over the generated bundle
- removal of old hardcoded Interop upgrade transaction files and bytecode fixtures
- op-e2e activation assertions for Interop state changes

## Draft status / known follow-ups

This is intentionally opened as a draft. Current known blockers before marking ready:

- `op-e2e/actions/proofs/nut_bundle_activation_test.go` still needs to compare against the full 30-tx Interop activation sequence, not just the 28 JSON bundle txs.
- Go/kona source-hash intent casing needs to be resolved for byte-identical bundle transactions.
- `go test ./op-e2e/actions/proofs -run "TestActivationBlockNUTBundle" -count=1` currently fails before reaching the new assertions because generated op-e2e contract bindings/artifacts are stale: `ReadImplementationAddressesOutput` has 19 Go fields while the ABI has 18.
- Cleanup remains: remove the empty committed `test` file, fix `git diff --check` blank-line-at-EOF in `op-e2e/actions/interop/interop_fork_test.go`, and clean up the temporary `test commit` commits.

## Verification so far

Passed:

```
go test ./op-node/rollup/derive/... -run "TestUpgradeTransactionsInterop|TestInteropSetFeatureTx|TestInteropETHLiquidityFundingTx|TestPreparePayloadAttributes/interop" -count=1
go test ./op-core/nuts/...
go test ./op-core/forks/...
```

Failed / blocked:

```
go test ./op-e2e/actions/proofs -run "TestActivationBlockNUTBundle" -count=1
```

Failure: stale generated binding/artifact mismatch in `ReadImplementationAddressesOutput`.

Not run: full contracts, kona, and full Go suites. `mise x` is blocked locally until this worktree's `mise.toml` is trusted.
